title: Sudan's Burhan Pledges Temporary Immunity for National Dialogue, Rules Out Hemedti's Return
detail: August 15, 2026 — Speaking at celebrations marking the 72nd anniversary of the Sudanese Armed Forces, Sovereignty Council chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan pledged temporary immunity and legal, political and security guarantees for participants in a proposed Sudanese national dialogue, saying criminal proceedings against participants would be temporarily suspended (without constituting a pardon) and that statements made during the sessions could not be used for prosecution. Burhan said the dialogue initiative was proposed independently by a group of Sudanese figures and that the state would not organize the process or dictate its agenda. He firmly ruled out any political comeback for RSF leader Mohamed 'Hemedti' Hamdan Dagalo, calling that path an 'incomplete peace,' and said the army would engage with serious peace initiatives only after RSF forces withdraw from cities they hold and displaced people return home.

title: African Union Peace and Security Council Delegation Arrives in Khartoum for Three-Day Visit
detail: August 15, 2026 — A delegation from the African Union Peace and Security Council, representing the council's 15 member states and led by Algeria (which holds the council's rotating August presidency), arrived in Khartoum for a three-day visit — its second since Sudan's civil war began and its first held in Khartoum itself rather than the wartime seat of Port Sudan. The delegation was scheduled to meet Sovereignty Council chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, Prime Minister Kamil Idris, political parties, and civil society organizations, as the AU seeks to strengthen its engagement on the Sudan file and support an inclusive political process alongside the national dialogue initiative Burhan endorsed the same day.

title: Venezuela Frees 131 More Prisoners Under Post-Maduro Reconciliation Program
detail: August 15, 2026 — Venezuela's interim government announced the release of 131 additional people held under the 'Program for Peace and Democratic Coexistence,' bringing the total freed since January 3 to over 1,046. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the release 'a crucial step for the nation's reconciliation process.' Rights group Foro Penal confirmed at least 40 of those freed were political prisoners, including Emirlendris Benitez, jailed over an alleged 2018 drone attack on then-president Maduro and documented as having been tortured in detention. The releases coincide with the US-brokered government-opposition transition talks that concluded their first round on August 12; Foro Penal estimates roughly 391 political prisoners remain incarcerated.
